title: Koszul-regular quotient as a derived tensor product
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $r\geq0$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$ be Koszul-regular in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let $P=\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ map to $R$ by $x_i\mapsto f_i$, let $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\subset P$, let $B=R/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, and let $\mathbf Z=P/J$. Then the canonical map $R\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}\mathbf Z\to B[0]$ is an isomorphism. Here the derived tensor is taken in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: it is the derived extension of scalars of $\mathbf Z[0]$ along $P\to R$, computed by a K-flat resolution of $\mathbf Z[0]$ over $P$ as in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor].

source.place: Tag 08SJ (lemma-mod-regular-sequence), proof: the Koszul resolution of $\mathbf Z$ over $P$ and the Koszul-regularity hypothesis after tensoring with $R$.

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq r$, setting $x_1,\ldots,x_i$ equal to zero gives $P/(x_1,\ldots,x_i)\simeq\mathbf Z[x_{i+1},\ldots,x_r]$: the discarded monomials are exactly those divisible by one of $x_1,\ldots,x_i$. For $i<r$, multiplication by $x_{i+1}$ on this quotient is injective, since it shifts the exponent of $x_{i+1}$ in the unique monomial expansion. At $i=r$ the quotient is $\mathbf Z$. These are the successive multiplication-injectivity hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] over $P$ with $M=P$. Applying it and identifying $K_P\otimes_P P=K_P$ makes the variables Koszul-regular, including the empty sequence.

source.place: Tag 08SJ (lemma-mod-regular-sequence), polynomial regular-sequence sentence; explicit coefficient verification

proof.text: Put $F(E)=\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_P R[0])$ with the $R$-action through $R[0]$, and let $Q_R$ be localization to $D(R)$. Apply [lem-trf-koszul-augmentation-kflat-model] to $A=P$, $S=R$, and $g_i=x_i$, whose Koszul-regularity was checked in step 1. It gives the bounded finite free K-flat quotient resolution $\epsilon_x:K_P\to\mathbf Z[0]$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:R\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_RF(K_P)$ satisfying $\eta_{\mathbf Z[0]}=Q_R(F(\epsilon_x))\circ\alpha$, where $\eta$ is the counit for the chosen derived extension of scalars. No $P$-flatness of $R$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08SJ (lemma-mod-regular-sequence), first proof paragraph: free Koszul resolution and derived tensor computation; its K-flat and counit details in more-algebra.tex, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism and section-derived-base-change (lemma-derived-base-change).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-koszul-augmented-scalar-extension] to $P\to R$ and the variables. Its quotient target is $B$, its map $\theta$ sends $\bar p\otimes a$ to $\overline{p(f)a}$, and its $\beta$ identifies the tensor resolution with $K_R(f)$ in $D(R)$. Write $\eta$ for the counit in step 2. The canonical arrow in the statement is $\mu=Q_R(\theta[0])\circ\eta_{\mathbf Z[0]}$. Substituting step 2 and the cited augmentation square gives $$\mu=Q_R(\theta[0])\circ Q_R(F(\epsilon_x))\circ\alpha=Q_R(\epsilon_f)\circ\beta\circ\alpha,$$ where $\epsilon_f:K_R(f)\to B[0]$ is the quotient augmentation.

source.place: Tag 062H (lemma-koszul-regular-flat-base-change), first identity in its proof, together with definition-koszul-complex and its differential formula; augmentation compatibility is the explicit wedge and balanced-quotient calculation.

proof.text: Place chain degree $q$ of $K_R(f)$ in cochain degree $-q$, as in steps 2 and 3. Koszul-regularity [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] gives $H^{-q}(K_R)=H_q(K_R)=0$ for $q\ne0$. By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], $H^0(K_R)=\operatorname{coker}(R^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{(f_i)}R)=B$, and $\epsilon_f$ induces the identity on this quotient. Thus $\epsilon_f:K_R\to B[0]$ induces isomorphisms in every cochain degree: it is a quasi-isomorphism, inverted by $Q_R$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The factorization in step 3 expresses $\mu$ as this isomorphism composed with $\beta$ and $\alpha$, so $\mu$ is invertible. For $r=0$, $K_R=R[0]$, the ideal is zero, and $\epsilon_f$ is the identity.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_comparison {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R) (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (ModuleCat.{u} (PolynomialRing.{u} r))] [HasDerivedCategory.{wR} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (PolynomialRing.{u} r)) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ L ⟶ ((ModuleCat.mixedTensor (polynomialMap f)).flip.map₂CochainComplex).flip.obj (ringComplex R) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) [L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} (PolynomialRing.{u} r)) (.up ℤ))] : IsIso (comparison f L ε)
lean.note: The canonical comparison is the left-derived counit followed by the explicit ordinary tensor/quotient isomorphism. L and ε quantify over the existing dependency interface, with its left-derived universal property; existence is supplied by lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor. The polynomial coefficient ring ULift ℤ is the universe-compatible copy of ℤ. All helpers belong to this canonical comparison.
